The detail file just adds an unconditional bullet ("Emit this instead of `BLOCKED` when splitting is the remedy"), so a create-side `apply_finding` can now return `BLOCKED-STRUCTURAL`, which create's loop (branching only on `APPLIED`) dead-ends and re-collects/re-dispatches every iteration until budget exhausts — exactly the leak the Open question says guard (a) prevents. — - `docs/implementation-plans/2-escalate-structural-findings-to-split.md`: rewrote the Open-question commitment from guard (a) to guard (b), explaining the static `apply-finding` prompt cannot be path-scoped and adding a create-side recommend-only catch for `BLOCKED-STRUCTURAL`.
- [APPLIED] Step 7's in-loop renumbering contract invalidates `target_steps` after a trigger-2 applied split ("the remaining `target_steps` entries carry pre-split ids and must not be processed") but never invalidates `mixed_steps`, which step 6's Phase-B `if mixed_steps:` block consumes *before* step 7's `if structural_split_ids:` re-author runs. When the same step K is both flagged `detail-purity` (appended to `mixed_steps`) and yields `BLOCKED-STRUCTURAL` on a separate `detail-body` apply (the same mixed-refactor+feature condition produces both), the trigger-2 split renumbers ids ≥ K, leaving the stale `mixed_steps` entry for K pointing at a freshly-created half; Phase B then runs `_split_is_safe`/`_propose_step_split` against that half — a spurious propose (wasted Claude on `--split` non-TTY) or a wrong-step `structural-split` recommendation. — - `docs/implementation-plans/plan-details/escalate-structural-findings-to-split/07-isolate-loop-renumbering-contract.md`: added a post-loop-block bullet stating a trigger-2 applied split also invalidates stale `mixed_steps` entries (ids ≥ split target), requiring Phase-B `mixed_steps` processing to be skipped or re-derived from the renumbered plan excluding `structural_split_ids` before the `if mixed_steps:` block consumes them.
- [APPLIED] The Deferred bullet ("Widening `completeness_report.py`'s blocked rollups") justifies excluding `BLOCKED-STRUCTURAL` by asserting it "is actively routed to the `escalate_to_split` bridge (steps 7/8) … so it never reaches the completeness summary as an unhandled split target." But the completeness *authoring-audit* loop (`completeness_cmd.py:cmd_completeness`) calls `apply_finding` directly (`completeness_cmd.py:1256`), dispatching its `partition_findings_for_triage` → `open_apply` set with the **same shared `prompts/apply-finding.md`** step 3 teaches to emit `BLOCKED-STRUCTURAL`; it branches only on `verdict != "APPLIED"` and is explicitly *not* wired to the bridge (Out of scope: "the completeness-apply walk"). Step 3's guard (a) scopes the prompt out of *create* only — it says nothing about completeness-apply — so a step that turns structural mid-apply here emits `BLOCKED-STRUCTURAL`, gets force-fit into the generic non-`APPLIED` note, has its fingerprint marked applied, and dead-ends exactly like the bare `BLOCKED` this plan set out to fix, on a path the Deferred rationale wrongly believes the bridge covers. — - `docs/implementation-plans/2-escalate-structural-findings-to-split.md`: rewrote the Deferred rollup-exclusion rationale to scope bridge routing to the detail loop and review/apply walk only, and to state the completeness-apply walk (`cmd_completeness`) treats `BLOCKED-STRUCTURAL` as bare-`BLOCKED` since it is out of scope and unwired to the bridge.
